ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier circuit. The op-amp supply rails are labeled +10V and -10V. The non-inverting input terminal (+) is directly connected to a +2V power source, and the lower end of this power source is grounded. The inverting input terminal (-) is connected to a resistor voltage-divider feedback network: from the inverting input node it is grounded through resistor R, and at the same time connected to the output terminal V0 through resistor 2R. Therefore this structure is a non-inverting amplifier, with feedback resistor 2R and grounding resistor R. Reasoning: Under linear negative feedback conditions, an ideal op-amp has V- = V+. Since V+ = 2V, the inverting terminal voltage V- = 2V. The inverting terminal is the node voltage obtained by dividing the output V0 through 2R and R, therefore V- = V0 × R / (2R + R) = V0 / 3. Let V0 / 3 = 2V, obtaining V0 = 6V. Checking the supply rails ±10V, 6V is within the allowable range, so the output will not saturate.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the op-amp as a non-inverting amplifier because the + input is tied to the +2 V source and the - input has a divider made of R to ground and 2R to the output. From the text, use the condition that the op-amp is ideal. Apply the ideal non-inverting gain formula: V0 = (1 + 2R/R)(2 V) = 6 V. Check against the shown ±10 V rails; since 6 V is allowed, the output is 6 V.

planner_metadata.image_role: Read the circuit topology: the op-amp output is fed back to the inverting input through a resistor labeled 2R, the inverting input is connected to ground through a resistor labeled R, the non-inverting input is driven by a +2 V source, and the supply rails are marked ±10 V with output labeled V0.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement's condition that the op-amp is ideal and that the requested quantity is the output voltage V0.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For an ideal op-amp with negative feedback, the non-inverting amplifier closed-loop gain is V0/V+ = 1 + Rf/Rg, provided the result is within the supply rails. Here Rf=2R and Rg=R, so the gain is 3; 3×2 V = 6 V, which is within ±10 V, so no saturation occurs.
